n: Inspired by the Passover, the worshippers went out and destroyed idols, Asherah poles, high places, and altars across Judah, Benjamin, and even Ephraim and Manasseh. Worship led to action. Then they returned home.
Hezekiah reorganized the priests and Levites into their rotating divisions, each with his duties — sacrifice, ministry, thanksgiving, and praise at the gates of the Lord’s house.

f.g: The temple, called by the old tabernacle term.

n: The king contributed from his own wealth for the daily, Sabbath, new moon, and festival burnt offerings, as the law required. Leaders give first.

f.w: as it is written in the law of the LORD

n: He commanded Jerusalem’s residents to give the priests’ and Levites’ portion, so these servants could devote themselves fully to God’s law.

f.w: that they might be encouraged in the law
f.g: That they could be devoted (literally ‘strong’) in the law, free from other labor.

n: As soon as the order went out, Israel generously brought firstfruits of grain, wine, oil, honey, and produce, and abundant tithes of everything.
Those living in Judah’s towns brought tithes of cattle and sheep and holy gifts, piling them up in heaps.

f.g: In piles — so much it had to be stacked.

n: They began piling up offerings in the third month (harvest of grain) and finished in the seventh (harvest of fruit and grapes).

f.g: Around the Feast of Weeks and wheat harvest.
Around the Feast of Tabernacles and fruit harvest.

n: When Hezekiah and the officials saw the heaps, they praised the Lord and blessed His people.
Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the heaps.
Azariah the chief priest explained: since the offerings began, we’ve had plenty to eat with lots left over, because the Lord has blessed His people. A fulfillment of God’s promise for tithing.

f.w: we have had enough to eat, and have left plenty

n: Hezekiah ordered storerooms prepared in the temple.
The offerings, tithes, and dedicated gifts were brought in faithfully, managed by the Levite Cononiah and his brother Shimei.
Ten overseers worked under them, appointed by the king and the chief priest. Careful organization ensured sacred funds were handled well.
Kore, gatekeeper of the East Gate, was in charge of freewill offerings and distributing the most holy portions.
Assistants in the priests’ towns faithfully distributed portions to their fellow priests by divisions, to old and young alike.

f.w: the great as to the small
f.g: Older and younger, or higher and lower rank.

n: They also gave daily portions to males three years and older registered in the genealogies who entered the temple for service.

f.g: Official family registers that determined priestly eligibility.

n: Distribution followed the genealogies of priests by families and Levites twenty and older by their duties.
Their whole families — wives, sons, daughters, little ones — were included, because they had consecrated themselves faithfully.

f.g: Kept themselves dedicated in their trusted service.

n: Men were also appointed in every priestly town and its pasturelands to distribute portions to all priests and registered Levites.
Hezekiah did this throughout Judah, doing what was good, right, and faithful before the Lord.
In everything he undertook for God’s house, law, and commandments, he sought God wholeheartedly — and he prospered. Wholehearted effort is the Chronicler’s formula for blessing.

f.w: he did it with all his heart, and prospered
